caveats: Small, throttle-dominated sample (30 units/config; 55-80% throttle at concurrency>=2 on the intercepted path).
'effective_certified_units_per_hour' is noisy: with few certified units and short elapsed, per-hour extrapolation is unstable (the c3 2413/hr figure is such an artifact and is NOT claimed).
Correctness is proven separately (native certify, cache reuse, no double cert, SIGTERM/resume, adaptive up/down); this artifact is about throughput only.
honest_conclusion: Parallel HTTP/2 is CORRECT and, in favorable network windows (p50 latency ~0.2s), far faster than the 55 units/hr serial baseline. But the intercepted corporate path throttles 55-80% of requests at concurrency>=2, so sustained throughput is variable and retry-dominated (amplification 4-7.5x). Conservative full-remaining ETA on THIS network: a few days (~3-5), a clear improvement over ~25 days serial but not hours. A non-intercepted permitted network (p50<1s, concurrency 4-8) would reach hours with this same runner.
